title: Reset failure
summary: A failed reset receipt names its failure: a check row's name and ok come from the operation, never nested evidence. When the server refuses a receipt, test_machine_operation_submit_failed repeats the host's error code, reason and recovery. A failed macOS reset keeps its first error code, and failed_calls records each failed call's exit code and bounded stderr, or its exception type and message; the runner's own SSH failure (exit 124) is test_mac_reset_transport_failed. Reset first finds each identity browser main process with /bin/ps -U USER and awk (argv holds --user-data-dir=$HOME/.yoke-browser-identities/ and no --type=), sends it SIGTERM, Chromium's clean shutdown that flushes cookies, and waits up to 30 seconds; it never force-kills. Sign-in refusals stop before anything is cleared: test_machine_sign_in_app_quit_not_proved when an identity browser is still running (close its windows at the console, then retry; never force-quit), and test_machine_sign_in_app_probe_failed when the process probe fails (check SSH, then retry). Reset then refuses test_machine_reset_console_user_mismatch, quitting nothing, unless the console user is the test user. It lists the test user's foreground apps with lsappinfo list and quits every one except Finder, the identity browsers, Docker Desktop and Tailscale (the reset's SSH runs over its tunnel, so quitting it cut a reset off from its host), matched by bundle ID and named in gui_apps_kept, killing an app's process tree when a sheet holds its quit; gui_apps_quit records each app as graceful or forced. These refusals also stop before clearing: test_machine_gui_app_list_failed when the listing fails or shows no GUI session, test_machine_gui_app_quit_not_proved when an app survives its quit and a forced kill (quit it in Activity Monitor at the console), and test_machine_gui_app_probe_failed when pgrep fails. An SSH timeout right after a GUI-app quit means the host left the tailnet: relaunch Tailscale at the console, confirm tailscale status shows it online, then retry. A Claude desktop probe that cannot quit the app it opened fails probe_app_quit_blocked, whose recovery is a reset, not a reinstall. System Events is stopped after the apps before clearing the home: test_machine_system_events_probe_failed means its process state could not be read; test_machine_system_events_quit_not_proved means it survived graceful quit and forced tree termination. Repair SSH/process access for an unreadable probe, or quit System Events in Activity Monitor at the host console, then retry reset. After a successful restore the reset relaunches Terminal without saved windows; test_machine_terminal_relaunch_failed means no window appeared. A harness probe whose reply the parser rejected keeps a sanitized reply_rejection record (rejection branch, event types, final event shape, exact-OK/tool-use/degraded-context booleans, harness exit code; never reply text) on its failed row; a QA run stores it as a probe_reply_rejection artifact and names the branch in its verdict reason. A golden sealed before these records returns none and its reason asks for a recapture. A Linux golden archive command that exits nonzero, including a timeout, keeps transport_diagnostics in its receipt with private SSH client debug and sshd journal log paths, the operation window and journal collection status. Collection uses the existing SSH transport and a bounded noninteractive journal read. A command that exits 0 removes its log folder, skips the journal read and records only status command_succeeded with the operation window. Inspect these logs before attributing SSH exit 255; an unavailable journal or warning alone does not prove a cause. Command payloads and capability secrets are redacted from retained logs. macOS reset emits success counters only after final process validation. A final-gate failure begins with the existing reap_processes phase marker and retains surviving reap failures and matching processes in process_state. Host load is not a reset condition. This source correction does not diagnose historical failures, recover lost stdout or goldens, or prove a live host repair.
